# opencodecounts <img src="man/figures/logo-hex.png" align="right" height="139" alt="OpenCodeCounts"/>

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/bennettoxford/opencodecounts/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bennettoxford/opencodecounts/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

The `opencodecounts` R package provides easy access to yearly summaries of clinical code usage in England.
The package makes NHS England's published datasets available in R and an interactive online tool, covering SNOMED CT codes in primary care and ICD-10/OPCS-4 codes in secondary care.

You can launch the interactive Shiny app by clicking on [Launch Shiny App](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/articles/app.html). For work in R, all available functions are documented in the [Function reference](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/reference/index.html) section.

## Installation

You can install the `opencodecounts` package in R with:  

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("bennettoxford/opencodecounts")
```

## How-to guides

- [How to use the Shiny app](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/articles/how-to-use-shiny-app.html)
- [How to use the R package](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/articles/how-to-use-R-pkg.html)
- [How to use ICD-10 and OPCS-4 breakdowns](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/articles/how-to-use-breakdowns.html)
- [How to extract semantic tags from SNOMED CT descriptions](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/articles/extract-snomedct-sem-tag.html)

## Available datasets

```{r datasets-info, include = FALSE}
dataset_info <- list(
  list(
    id = "gp_snomed", 
    fn = "get_gp_snomed()", 
    desc = "GP records, SNOMED CT", 
    data = get_gp_snomed()
  ),
  list(
    id = "hesapc_icd10", 
    fn = "get_hesapc_icd10()", 
    desc = "HES Admitted Patient Care, ICD-10 diagnoses", 
    data = get_hesapc_icd10()
  ),
  list(
    id = "hesapc_icd10_breakdowns", 
    fn = "get_hesapc_icd10_breakdowns()", desc = "HES Admitted Patient Care, ICD-10 diagnoses, with breakdowns",
    data = get_hesapc_icd10_breakdowns()
  ),
  list(
    id = "hesapc_opcs4", 
    fn = "get_hesapc_opcs4()", 
    desc = "HES Admitted Patient Care, OPCS-4 procedures", 
    data = get_hesapc_opcs4()
  ),
  list(
    id = "hesapc_opcs4_breakdowns", 
    fn = "get_hesapc_opcs4_breakdowns()", 
    desc = "HES Admitted Patient Care, OPCS-4 procedures, with breakdowns", 
    data = get_hesapc_opcs4_breakdowns()
  )
)

dataset_dates <- purrr::map_dfr(dataset_info, function(d) {
  tibble::tibble(
    id = d$id,
    start = min(d$data$start_date),
    end = max(d$data$end_date)
  )
})

gp_dates <- dplyr::filter(dataset_dates, startsWith(id, "gp"))
gp_start <- format(min(gp_dates$start), "%Y-%m-%d")
gp_end <- format(max(gp_dates$end), "%Y-%m-%d")

hes_dates <- dplyr::filter(dataset_dates, startsWith(id, "hesapc"))
hes_start <- format(min(hes_dates$start), "%Y-%m-%d")
hes_end <- format(max(hes_dates$end), "%Y-%m-%d")
```

The table below lists every dataset in the `opencodecounts` R package, with links to download the tidy data as Parquet files.
GP data covers `r gp_start` to `r gp_end`, and HES data covers `r hes_start` to `r hes_end`.
Read the vignette for more on each dataset: [Available datasets in opencodecounts](https://bennettoxford.github.io/opencodecounts/articles/available-datasets.html).

```{r datasets-table, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
tidy_sources <- load_tidy_sources_config()

purrr::map_dfr(dataset_info, function(d) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Function = paste0("`", d$fn, "`"),
    Description = paste0(d$desc, " (v", tidy_sources[[d$id]]$version, ")"),
    `Tidy data` = paste0("[Download](", tidy_sources[[d$id]]$url, ")")
  )
}) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "l"))
```
